TSMC manufactures Apple's custom chips, while OpenAI and Anthropic are developing processors of their own. items.title: AMD’s Venice-X maxes out family at 5.3 GHz, returning 3D V-Cache to data center after four years
items.snippet: AMD's Venice-X CPUs launch in the second half of 2027, bringing 3D V-Cache back to the data center after four years on the sidelines.

items.title: PC peripheral maker Logitech giving all of its 7,000 employees the day off to play GTA 6
items.snippet: Accessory maker Logitech has a new "Logi Game Day" initiative that allows employees to take a day off from now until this time next year to play a game of their choice — including the one everyone is talking about.

items.title: SpaceX develops its own ‘Kessel’ rack-scale system featuring 72 Nvidia Rubin GPUs for data centers in space, report claims
items.snippet: SpaceX is reportedly developing a 'Kessel' rack-scale system design with 72 Nvidia Rubin GPUs that relies on a massive 84-layer PCB midplane.

items.title: ASRock quietly rolls out new firmware after disastrous previous update killed Radeon RX 7900-series GPUs
items.snippet: Asrock's VBIOS 1.0.6 update follows reports of Radeon RX 7900 XT and XTX graphics cards failing to boot after installing the previous firmware.

items.title: Montech King 95 3D Pro case review: The King has returned
items.snippet: The new Montech King 95 3D case offers 3-panel panoramic views of the inside, loads of interior space for components and cooling, and the Pro version comes with seven RGB fan

items.title: Cognichip reveals how its new AI-assisted program can slash chip design times from months to days — automating labor-intensive tasks cuts design time down, Chief Product Officer explains
items.snippet: Cognichip claims its AI can slash chip design time from months to days, only that that design must be very simplistic.

items.title: Congress could issue subpoena to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang if he doesn’t respond by today to request for a ‘joint, closed-door briefing’
items.snippet: Three committee chairpersons want to grill Jensen Huang about his company's 'security protocols against foreign adversary espionage,' as a former CIA agent says that he had a target on his back as the leader of a trillion-dollar company.

items.title: Cyanogen co-founder unveils Kora, a Linux OS that splits AI models across the CPU, GPU, and NPU
items.snippet: Kora, a Linux desktop OS with built-in AI models and agents for local agentic work, is coming to PCs in 2027, including Snapdragon X2 Elite machines.

items.title: AMD shares how it can retain 95% of server performance with just half the DRAM, sidestepping memory shortages with MEXT
items.snippet: Following AMD’s acquisition of MEXT earlier this year, the company has revealed its own IT infrastructure is using the technology to run servers at 50% DRAM capacity while achieving 95% of the performance of a full-DRAM system in certain applications.

items.title: Grab 32GB DDR5 for $351 with this Newegg bundle with the 9800X3D, $87 less than the next cheapest memory
items.snippet: Another brilliant Newegg combo deal has combined the eight-core AMD Ryzen 7 9850X3D with 32GB of V-Color DDR5-6400 RAM, all for just $650, saving you a whopping $348.99 in the process.

items.title: Modder routes PC water cooling loop to radiator outside to beat the winter heat
items.snippet: A Reddit PC builder didn't want to bother opening a window in the winter when their system made their legs too hot, so they created an automated split cooling system to dump heat outside.

items.title: AMD VP and chief Zen architect rebuke claims that Nvidia and Arm made CPUs for agentic AI — ‘We didn’t magically know four years ago that agentic was going to be a thing’
items.snippet: Nvidia and Arm have new “agentic CPUs,” a title that high-ranking AMD employees are pushing back against with the launch of Zen 6 EPYC Venice CPUs.

items.title: AMD Zen 6 EPYC ‘Venice’ deep dive and benchmarking
items.snippet: AMD has pulled back the curtain on its Zen 6 microarchitecture. We deep-dive into the differences between Zen 5 and 6, as well as detail our first benchmarks of AMD’s Venice CPUs.

items.title: Alice Huang reportedly instrumental in securing over $7.5 billion of Nvidia AI GPU imports during three-year relationship with Jensen Huang
items.snippet: Alice Huang is reportedly connected to a web of Chinese companies, which then leveraged her closeness to Jensen Huang to gain access to billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia GPUs.

items.title: Secretlab debuts monitor light bar add-on to reduce glare and eye strain

items.title: Seagate resurrects hybrid storage: Hands-on with the FireCuda Forge – 8 or 20TB external hard drive requires you to bring your own NVMe SSD

It's a throwback to the days of hybrid drives, and the experience is pretty seamless once you install your SSD. But if you don't already own an SSD that you can drop in, it's still quite expensive.

items.title: Launching the Vite Ecosystem Fund
items.snippet: Cloudflare is distributing the first $301,300 of the Vite Ecosystem Fund to 44 projects and maintainers across the Vite ecosystem. When VoidZero joined Cloudflare, we committed $1 million to strengthen the open source ecosystem around Vite. This round is just the start. Sponsoring open source has always mattered, but now AI has made funding urgent. AI has made open source more valuable while triggering more maintainer burnout. Previously, contributing to a project through either an issue or pull request meant you cared about it. In return, maintainers would review and provide feedback. AI changed the social contract of open source. Anyone can now create and submit AI-authored pull requests. The most visible result is the influx of pull requests. As the number of PRs has gone up, the number of maintainers reviewing them has stayed constant. So each maintainer’s workload has grown. During reviews, maintainers often find themselves speaking with an agent and not a person like they used to. If that’s the case, then why not cut out the middleman?
